newsitem.title: UK: Brown sees UK inflation at 2.5 pct in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Brown sees UK inflation at 2.5 pct in 1997.

text.p: Britain's Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown on Wednesday forecast that underlying retail price inflation would run at 2.5 percent year-on-year in 1997 and 2.75 percent in 1998.
In 1999 he sees it at 2.5 percent.

"Inflation is expected to remain at 2.5 percent this year, the government's target, rising slightly to 2.75 percent next year as a result of the failure by the last government to take early action to control inflation," he told parliament in his budget speech.
The government has a medium-term target of 2.5 percent for underlying inflation, which excludes volatile home loan payments.
In last November's budget, Brown's predecessor, Kenneth Clarke, forecast RPIX at 2.5 percent this year and in the first half of 1998.
The Bank of England, now independent to set interest rates, is responsible for keeping inflation under control and has warned that the consumer sector represents a threat to the inflation outlook.

British interest rates have been increased by 1/4 percentage point in each of the past two months and some pundits are looking for a further rise on July 10, at the end of the monetary policy committee's next meeting.
(A separate summary of key economic forecasts will be issued after Brown finishes his budget speech.)
